content: The interaction between erythromycin base and inhaled insulin results in a pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to an enhanced glucose-lowering effect. Both drugs decrease blood glucose levels, so caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and irinotecan liposomal by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2E1 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Erythromycin base increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Istradefylline increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. At a dose of 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Istradefylline also increases erythromycin base levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates should be considered. Erythromycin base increases itraconazole levels or effects by inhibiting both hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base elevates ivacaftor levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Ivacaftor dose reduction is recommended when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-gp, potentially increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Erythromycin base increases ivermectin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base elevates ivosidenib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, raising the risk of QTc prolongation. Monitoring for QTc interval prolongation is necessary. Erythromycin base increases ketoconazole levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole also increases erythromycin base levels via the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base elevates lapatinib levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Both erythromycin base and lapatinib prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Erythromycin base increases larotrectinib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Lenacapavir increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels for up to 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Both erythromycin base and lenvatinib prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Lenvatinib prescribing information advises close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. Erythromycin base increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Letermovir also increases erythromycin base levels via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Leuprolide increases erythromycin base toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Erythromycin base elevates levamlodipine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially necessitating dose reduction. Monitor for hypotension and edema symptoms. Both erythromycin base and levofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Levoketoconazole increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin base also increases levoketoconazole levels via the same mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base decreases levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Lomitapide increases erythromycin base levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Dose reduction should be considered when used concomitantly with lomitapide. Erythromycin base elevates loperamide levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lorlatinib decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base increases lumateperone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Erythromycin base elevates lurasidone levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The manufacturer recommends reducing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Concurrent use may increase the risk of lurasidone-related adverse reactions. Erythromycin base increases maraviroc levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base elevates mavacamten levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. Erythromycin base increases mavorixafor levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Mavorixafor prolongs the QTc interval in a concentration-dependent manner. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Erythromycin base elevates mefloquine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base decreases mestranol levels or effects by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral hormone forms. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin base also increases mestranol levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Both erythromycin base and methadone prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Erythromycin base increases methylprednisolone levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates mifepristone levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Alternatives should be used if available. Mipomersen and erythromycin base both increase each other's toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). Mitotane decreases erythromycin base levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. Erythromycin base increases mitoxantrone levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base increases momelotinib toxicity. Caution and monitoring are necessary. OATP1B1/B3 inhibition elevates momelotinib plasma concentrations, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Erythromycin base elevates montelukast levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base increases naldemedine levels via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Monitor for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Erythromycin base elevates nelfinavir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base increases neomycin PO levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base decreases niacin levels or effects by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral form of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates nifedipine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Consider initiating nifedipine at the lowest dose available if given concomitantly. Erythromycin base increases nilotinib levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates nimodipine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base increases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. Nirmatrelvir increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor for increased erythromycin adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir elevates erythromycin base levels via hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. Monitor for increased erythromycin adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. Erythromycin base increases nitrendipine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates norgestrel levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. Both erythromycin base and ofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Erythromycin base increases oliceridine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Both erythromycin base and olodaterol inhaled prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Both osilodrostat and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Both osimertinib and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Conduct periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. Oxaliplatin increases erythromycin base levels or effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Erythromycin base elevates oxybutynin levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Both ozanimod and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. Erythromycin base increases paclitaxel levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates paclitaxel protein-bound levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. Erythromycin base increases palbociclib levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Erythromycin base elevates paliperidone levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Both erythromycin base and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval.
